title: Definitions and method
lede: Every figure in this catalog is stated with the condition under which it applies. Bigframe publishes repeatability, and the method with it.
def1_desc: The sensor grid: the maximum number of points one capture can return.
def2_desc: Camera reference plane to the part. Every model is specified at the near, optimum and far working distance.
def3_desc: Measured width × height at a stated working distance.
def4_desc: Near to far working distance: the depth over which the camera returns points.
def5_desc: Field of view at the optimum working distance × the depth over which the stated figures hold.
def6_desc: Distance between neighboring points at the optimum working distance: a sampling pitch, not the smallest resolvable feature.
def7_desc: Repeatability of the height difference between two adjacent areas over 100 captures; the largest 2σ found is printed.
def8_desc: 3D frames per second at the stated resolution.
fig_caption: The reference plate at the near, optimum and far working distance. Illustration.
method_text: A ceramic reference plate is imaged at the near, optimum and far working distance. The field of view is divided into nine regions; in each, two adjacent areas of under 1 % of the field are measured. The difference of their mean heights is measured 100 times; its standard deviation is the regional repeatability (1σ). Twice that value (2σ), the largest across nine regions and three distances, is the printed figure.
plan_caption: Nine regions; A and B adjacent in each
aside_text: The figure is the repeatability of a difference of two area means: the standard deviation of A − B over 100 captures (1σ), printed as 2σ. It is smaller than the repeatability of a single point, which is not published.
why_text: Repeatability is one component of measurement uncertainty and can be stated for the camera alone, on a stated method. Whether a camera holds a tolerance is decided on the part, by a gauge study; the figures here select the model to start with.
where_text: Series pages 5–14: models at a glance and fields of view. Page 17: all eighteen models on one table. Pages 18–20: full specification per series; page 21: cables and calibration targets.
